findings.title: Team authorization requires users to be both admin and owner
findings.body: The team permission check joins `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so a team admin who is not also an owner is rejected. This prevents the team-admin role from using the endpoint even though the booking UI treats admins and owners as authorized. Use an OR between the role checks.

findings.title: Guest email normalization lets callers bypass the blacklist
findings.body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. Because email validation does not lowercase addresses, a caller can submit a blacklisted address with different casing and have it inserted and sent invitations. Normalize both sides before checking; the same normalization should be used when detecting existing attendees.

findings.title: A calendar sync failure leaves guests inserted but prevents notifications
findings.body: The database attendee update has already committed before this external calendar update runs. If the update throws, the mutation fails before sending any emails, but the guests remain in the database; retrying those addresses then finds no new guests and errors. The operation can therefore leave guests added without calendar updates or invitations, with no way to recover through the same request. Handle this partial-failure case, for example by making retries idempotent and ensuring notifications/sync can be retried.

findings.title: The endpoint allows guests to be added to cancelled bookings
findings.body: The handler never checks the booking status, so an authorized attendee can call this mutation for a cancelled or rejected booking even though the UI only offers the action for confirmed bookings. The new attendee is then sent a scheduled email with a confirmed calendar invitation for an event that is no longer active. Reject bookings that are not in an eligible status on the server.

findings.title: Add-guest notifications ignore event-type email-disable settings
findings.body: Unlike the other booking email senders, this function does not check the event type's `disableStandardEmails` settings. Adding guests therefore sends host and attendee notifications even when standard emails are disabled for that event type, defeating the configured preference. Apply the host and attendee disable checks here as well.
